questions.prompt: Which sequence of notifications is allowed by the Observable contract?

options.text: next, next, complete
next, complete, next
complete, error
next, error, complete

questions.explanation: The grammar is next* (error | complete)? — any number of next values, then at most one terminal notification, with nothing after it. Only 'next, next, complete' fits.

questions.prompt: You subscribe to the same cold Observable (which fetches `/api/data`) twice. How many requests fire?

options.text: Two — each subscription runs the producer independently
One — subscriptions share a single execution
Zero — Observables never run producers automatically
It depends on the network cache only

questions.explanation: Plain Observables are cold/unicast: each subscribe() re-runs the producer, so two subscriptions cause two requests. Sharing one execution requires multicasting.

questions.prompt: Which events cause the producer's returned teardown function to run? Select all that apply.

options.text: The stream completes
The stream errors
The consumer calls unsubscribe()
The Observable is created but never subscribed

questions.explanation: Teardown runs exactly once on the first of complete, error, or unsubscribe. A never-subscribed Observable does no work at all, so there is nothing to tear down.

questions.prompt: A producer calls `next(1)`, then `complete()`, then `next(2)`. What does the Observer receive?

options.text: next(1) and complete — the next(2) is ignored
next(1), complete, and next(2)
An error, because next after complete is illegal
Only next(2)

questions.explanation: After a terminal notification the subscriber is stopped and ignores further emissions. RxJS enforces the contract, so next(2) never reaches the Observer.

questions.prompt: A plain Observable that runs its producer independently for every subscriber is called ______ (the one-word term contrasted with 'hot').
questions.explanation: Cold (unicast) Observables run the producer per subscription. Hot Observables share a single producer/execution among subscribers.

questions.prompt: When does the producer function passed to `new Observable(fn)` first execute?

options.text: When something calls subscribe() on the Observable
Immediately when the Observable is constructed
On the next microtask after construction
Only when unsubscribe() is called

questions.explanation: Observables are lazy: the producer runs on subscribe(), not on construction. No subscribe means no work.
